This script reads the two data files and adds what the models and figures need: the weekly estimates with their intervals, the variables that describe the interrupted time series, and the dates used in Figure 2.

Only a person authorized to use the data runs it. The data are not in this repository, and nothing on this site comes from running it.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/prepare_data.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/prepare_data.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/COVID-infection-control/blob/main/R/functions.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/prepare_data.R")
```

## The weekly surveillance data

One row per week, with the number of healthcare personnel tested and the number positive, the number of hospital-acquired infections (possible and confirmed together; see the [analysis plan](analysis-plan.qmd), section 7) and the number of patient-days. The data are aggregate counts: no individual-level data were available or used.

The script checks that the seven columns the code expects are present, and stops if any is missing. The message names only the missing columns, never any values.

```{r}
#| label: read-surveillance-data
#| eval: false
```

## Time series variables

An interrupted time series model needs two things beyond the outcome: a time variable, and an indicator of whether each week falls after the intervention.

-   `Intervention` is `TRUE` from week 13, the first week with face shields.
-   `Week2` is the week number minus 13, so it is zero at the intervention week.

Centring the week at 13 does not change how well the model fits, or its predictions. It changes what the coefficients mean: with `Week2` zero at week 13, the `Intervention` coefficient becomes the difference between the predictions with and without the intervention *at week 13*, which is the comparison the article reports. That difference is on the model's scale: a difference in log-odds for test positivity, and in log rates for HAI. Exponentiated, it is an odds ratio or a rate ratio, not a difference in percentage points or in rates. Without centring, it would be that difference at week 0, which lies outside the study.

```{r}
#| label: add-time-series-variables
#| eval: false
```

## Plot dates

Figure 2 draws the weekly series by date, alongside daily Harris County cases, so each week needs a date. `Date2` is taken to be the last day of each week's range, as the author recalls; this is not documented in the data. On that reading it is a Friday, and two days before it is the Wednesday in the middle of the week. Week 1, which began on Friday 17 April, is drawn one day before its `Date2`, as in the original code.

#| label: add-plot-dates
